Personal Profile

Yingnan Zhang is an Assistant Professor and Ph.D. supervisor in the Department of Land Management, School of Public Affairs, Zhejiang University. He serves as Deputy Secretary-General of the Youth Working Committee of the Chinese Association of Land Management; Secretary-General of Zhejiang University’s Urbanization and Spatial Governance Research Center and the Human Geography Committee of the Zhejiang Geographical Society; a member of the Commission on Agricultural Geography and Rural Development of the Geographical Society of China and the Land Resources Committee of the Chinese Society of Natural Resources; Deputy Secretary-General of the Academic and Development Committee of the Chinese Research Institute of Construction Management (CRIOCM); and a researcher with the Mobile China Research Network at the China Development Institute, Shanghai Jiao Tong University. He is an Editorial Board Member of Journal of Rural Studies and Environmental Research: Food Systems, and Executive Editor of Journal of Urban Management. His research focuses on farmland protection and food security, rural spatial restructuring and governance, and rural land institutional reform. He has published more than 40 articles in international journals, including Nature Sustainability, Food Policy, Global Food Security, Landscape and Urban Planning, Geoforum, Rural Sociology, Journal of Rural Studies and Planning Theory & Practice. His work includes ESI Highly Cited Papers and articles reprinted in full in the scholarly reprint series published by Renmin University of China. His book publications span three Chinese- and English-language volumes, including a forthcoming monograph. Several of his policy advisory reports have been adopted by the General Office of the State Council or received written endorsements from provincial Party leadership. He has led General Program and Young Scientists Fund projects supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China. Selected as a Zhongying Young Scholar at Zhejiang University, he has received more than ten honours and awards, including the CAAPA Wen Wang Award for Best Young Scholar Paper (2025), the President’s Award of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the seventh Outstanding Scientific Paper Award of the China Association for Science and Technology, and recognition for outstanding contributions to the third-party evaluation of poverty alleviation outcomes, awarded by the State Council Leading Group of Poverty Alleviation and Development.

Research

Two connected lines of inquiry
01

Agricultural and food system transformation and governance

How do states, markets and farmers reshape agricultural production and food provision? I examine the consequences of land-use change for food security, environmental sustainability and agricultural equity.

Farmland transitionsFood governanceClimate & equity
02

Rural commodification and spatial restructuring

How do rural land, nature, culture and rurality acquire value and enter markets? I study how commodification reshapes places and livelihoods, and how its benefits and costs are distributed and governed.

Digital platformsRural restructuringSpatial governance

Chinese publications

  1. Development pathways and risk response measures for non-traditional cropland from the perspective of greater food approach

    李文博, 刘蜀涵, 祝元丽, 张英男*, 巩晓曦, 刘佳傲等 (2026)

    资源科学, 48 (01): 88-99

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The development of non-traditional cropland constitutes a crucial strategic initiative formulated by China based on its fundamental national conditions in the new era. This study employs inductive analysis and literature review methods to summarize the definition, development pathways, and potential risk response measures of non-traditional cropland, thereby providing theoretical support for the scientific formulation of development strategies. The results of this study show that non-traditional cropland refers to land or space that is difficult to develop and utilize through conventional farming practices. However, through technological innovation and resource integration, these constraints can be overcome, enabling their use for agricultural production. From the perspective of the greater food approach and using an integrated and expansive approach, this study summarizes the classified development pathways of non-traditional cropland, including enhancing the productive potential of degraded land, promoting diversified operation of other agricultural land, exploring the agricultural value of idle land, and conducting refined development of coastal tidal flats. Among these, secondary land degradation and environmental pollution are identified as potential negative effects in the development of non-traditional cropland, a process that is also constrained by high operational costs and resource management standards. The development of non-traditional cropland essentially integrates the “storing grain in technology” and“storing grain in land”strategies, accelerating the cultivation of new quality productive forces in agriculture. It is necessary to accurately define functional positioning and implement differentiated strategies by region and category based on the types of modern agriculture supported by non-traditional cropland.

    Published English abstract

  2. Non-Traditional Arable Land Use: Advances and Future Directions

    张英男, 徐小峰, 李文博 (2025)

    上海国土资源, 46 (04): 14-20

    Abstract

    Amid overlapping shocks from global trade disputes, local conflicts and extreme climate events, food systems are undergoing profound transformation. To address mounting food security challenges, non-traditional arable land resources are increasingly entering the agendas of policy-making and academic research. Building on a theoretical review, this study clarifes the concept of non-traditional arable land, synthesizes domestic and international research and practice, and outlines future research directions. Existing studies largely centre on related concepts such as edible landscapes, productive landscapes and urban agriculture, drawing mainly on case studies and feld surveys to explore resource identifcation and potential assessment, utilization patterns and exemplary practices, as well as benefit evaluation and impact analysis. However, the defnition and classifcation of non-traditional arable land remain ambiguous, particularly within urban community contexts where research is sparse. We argue that harnessing non-traditional arable land offers an innovative pathway to strengthen food security and advance urban sustainability. Future work should deepen inquiry into conceptual frameworks and classifcation standards, spatial planning and policy, technological innovation and sustainability, economic viability and business models, socio-cultural dimensions and public engagement, benefit assessment systems, and the implications of scaling for food security.

    Published English abstract

  3. Effectiveness Assessment and Long-Term Operation of Comprehensive Land Consolidation

    张英男, 王威, 孙政隆 (2025)

    中国土地, (12): 18-21

    Abstract

    Comprehensive land consolidation requires evaluation and operating arrangements that sustain benefits beyond project completion. This article argues for a shift from short-term project assessment toward long-term spatial governance. It examines limitations of existing evaluation systems and proposes a life-cycle approach linking project acceptance to subsequent operation and maintenance. Key measures include integrating remote sensing, sensors and field observations; using blockchain-based records to support traceability; connecting monitoring information through a unified spatial database; and designing modular indicators at national, provincial and project levels. Clear maintenance responsibilities and funding mechanisms are needed to preserve improvements to farmland, infrastructure, village environments and ecosystems.

    English overview

  4. Village Committee in Farmland Transfer: Roles, Behaviors and Optimization

    周梓悦, 张英男* (2025)

    中国土地科学, 39 (11): 78-87

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The purposes of this study are to analyze the behavioral logic of village committees in farmland transfer and to explore pathways for optimizing their positive roles, to promote farmland transfer that integrates efficiency, equity, and sustainability. The research methods are as follows. Drawing on a literature review, the study develops a theoretical framework of“structural role-space for agency-behavioral choices and differentiated transfer outcomes”and conducts induction and deduction. The research results show that: 1）the dual logic of farmland transfer policies, together with the tension between government and villager’s preferences, generates inherent conflicts in village committees’role as “dual agents”. 2）Transformations in organizational structure of rural community and the discretionary power in policy implementation provide village committees with a certain degree of agency, which enables them to navigate structural role conflicts by seeking a balance among government objectives, collective interests, and rural households’demands. 3）In the context of weak public participation, the village committees’strategy of emphasizing expansive policies while neglecting protective ones often result in compulsory transfers. By contrast, in the context of strong public participation, the flexible implementation of farmland transfer policies with varying expansive and protective intensity allows rigid policies to achieve a“soft landing”in rural settings or exposes their limitations. In conclusion, the optimization of village committees’roles and behaviors in farmland transfer should be guided by the promotion of voluntary farmland transfers consistent with market principles, and by the development of diverse cooperative mechanisms that link the interests of rural households. By reforming accountability mechanisms—such as improving performance measurement, strengthening channels for public feedback, and enhancing both internal and external supervision— village committees can perform their functions of service coordination and management, serving as reliable bridges connecting government, markets, and rural households.

    Published English abstract

  5. Mechanism and implications of comprehensive land consolidation in promoting village revitalization: Taking Dongheng Village in Deqing County, Zhejiang Province as an example

    姜棪峰, 罗丹艺, 张英男* (2025)

    资源科学, 47 (01): 97-109

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    [Objective] Comprehensive land consolidation, as a systematic project for territorial spatial adjustment and optimization, is being widely used to alleviate rural issues and promote sustainable development of villages. The village, being the fundamental unit of rural planning and development, serves as an ideal scale to provide scientific basis for the practice of optimizing and adjusting rural territorial space. [Methods] Based on the theoretical analysis of the relationship between comprehensive land consolidation and village revitalization, this study takes Dongheng Village in Deqing County, Zhejiang Province as an example to carry out an empirical study, aiming to reveal the mechanism by which comprehensive land consolidation influences the revitalization of rural villages. [Results] (1) Under the combined influence of internal and external factors, the comprehensive land consolidation project, based on the policy system and engineering technology, drives the restructuring of rural spaces and the layout adjustment of development factors by promoting the synergistic development of different subsystems, thus contributing to village revitalization. (2) Under the joint effect of internal and external factors such as policy support, industrial foundation, resource endowment, and cooperation among rural elites, the comprehensive land consolidation project in Dongheng Village has been carried out smoothly. (3) By using comprehensive land consolidation as a platform, Dongheng Village promoted talent development, land efficiency, and industrial transformation by constructing a multi-dimensional subsystem linkage mechanism centered on governance innovation, which led to eco-friendly, intensification and high-value development of the production, living and ecological spaces, and ultimately achieved village transformation and revitalization. [Conclusion] Regions with conditions should fully utilize the role of rural elites both within and outside the administrative system and carry out comprehensive land consolidation programs tailored to local conditions, and, on this basis, promote these programs as platforms for connecting regional policies, land engineering, infrastructure construction, industrial development, and villagers’employment. This approach can enhance their demonstrative effect and further advance rural revitalization from village level to regional level.

    Published English abstract

  6. Greenhouse-mulched farmland transition: Theory and progress

    张英男,吴岚,余黎,龙花楼,李文博 (2024)

    地理研究, 43 (02): 519-534

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The purpose of this study is to review the existing research on the protected agriculture- induced farmland transition, offer guidance for future research, and develop a theory of protected agriculture- driven farmland transition. Methods of documentation and induction analysis were employed. The research results show that (1) The transition of farmland caused by protected agriculture is a rational decision for farmers who want to use greenhouse technology to address the scarcity of land resources. Its fundamental procedure entails increasing the intense margin relying on agricultural technology improvement. (2) The current research continues to use the classic measuring techniques for farmland transition indicators, concentrating on scale and structure indicators in the dominant morphology and giving more attention to input, output, price, etc. in the recessive morphology. (3) Due to data gathering limitations and other issues, a precise description of the spatiotemporal protected agriculture- induced farmland transition is currently missing from the standpoint of spatiotemporal evolution. In the absence of micro-scale investigations, the majority of current research examines the macro-scale protected agriculture-induced farmland change using remote sensing or statistical data. Its environmental and socio-economic factors have been extensively studied using econometric approaches, and mechanism analysis is still done at the macroregional level. (4) There is a lack of a complete investigation of its multifaceted consequences from a comprehensive perspective, and the analysis of its economic or environmental repercussions is frequently constrained to a single perspective of agricultural economics or environmental science. This paper concludes that future research should expand on the micro-mechanism of protected agriculture's influence on farmland transition, innovate “environmental- economic”benefit trade- off analysis theories and methods, and investigate ways to transform farmland use in a sustainable and intensive manner. It should also support sustainable farmland use.

    Published English abstract

  7. Resilience of Food Systems: Relocalized Transition of Cultivated Land Use in the City-region

    李文博,闫卓冉,张英男*,祝元丽,刘蜀涵,李冬梅 (2023)

    中国土地科学, 37 (11): 63-72

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The purposes of this study are to investigate the pathways for the relocalized transition of cultivated land use in the city-region, and to build the resilience of food systems, serving as a theoretical basis for ensuring the supply of agricultural products and the high-quality urbanization development. The research methods include inductive deduction and literature review. The results indicate that, 1）short-term recovery and long-term sustainability are crucial to improving the resilience of city-region food systems（CRFS）, and the key is to make prudent trade-offs between global and local supply, and properly shorten the supply chain. 2）The foreign experience suggests to use incremental prevention and potential mining to reactivate cultivated land in and around the cities, and most practices are dominated by planning constraints and supported by economic incentives. In China, the relocalization of cultivated land use in the city-region is mainly constrained by insufficient motivation, lack of planning, and limited elastic optimization. 3）The relocalized transition of cultivated land use includes three levels. Following the land-saving principle, we should preserve, reclaim, and create agricultural space within the city. Rigid constraints should be turned into structural and functional regulation around the city. Rural hinterlands, however, should be provided with optimized production base systems to decentralize risks and equilibrate production and demand. In conclusion, to achieve the relocalized transition of cultivated land use in the city-region, traditional urban-rural dichotomy shall be broken, and an integrated city-agriculture relationship shall be restructured. In this transition, coordination between the baseline of food security and effective supply of important agricultural products, high-quality urbanization and modern agricultural development, rigid control and flexible regulation of cultivated land is required.

    Published English abstract

  8. Theory and Practice of County-level Territorial Space Planning under the Context of Urban-Rural Integrated Development

    张英男, 龙花楼* (2023)

    中国土地科学, 37(02):1-10

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The purpose of this paper is to investigate how to use the policy tool of territorial space planning to support the county-level urban-rural integration development, to deepen and enrich the theoretical understanding and practical innovation of territorial space planning against the backdrop of urban-rural integration. The research methods of literature review and inductive deduction are employed. The results are as follows. First, this paper interprets the theoretical insight that territorial space planning empowers the integrated development of county-level urban and rural areas and proposes the optimization of the hierarchical system of central places, the rational flow of regional factors, and the integration of urban and rural areas, which is based on the theory of polarization effect and diffusion effect, the theory of“the space of flows”and the theory of reciprocal urban-rural development. Second, the practice paths of territorial space governance for“integration”,“suburbanization”and“centralization”are proposed, based on regional variances and three types of counties in metropolitan areas, hinterland of great cities, and distant fringe areas, respectively. In conclusion, the core of spatial governance for urban-rural integration is the judicious application of territorial space planning to support the diffusion effect of regional development and direct the two-way movement of urban and rural factors to create a mutually beneficial urban-rural network system, thereby fostering the county-level urban-rural integrated development.

    Published English abstract

  9. Classification of the coupling patterns between agricultural production system transition and their environmental effects in the plain farming regions

    张英男, 龙花楼*, 李裕瑞, 马历 (2022)

    地理研究, 41(06):1623-1636

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The green transformation of agriculture has become an inevitable choice of rural vitalization and agricultural/rural reforms, and exploring the relationship between agricultural production system transition and its environmental effects is urgently needed, thus fueling the high-quality development. Based on the typological method, this paper divides the agricultural transition models into the transformation from traditional management into modern agriculture in suburban regions and the transformation from traditional management into modern intensive agriculture in exurb regions. The agricultural production patterns in plain regions can be classified into modern intensive agriculture in suburban regions, traditional management agriculture in suburban regions, modern intensive agriculture in exurb regions, and traditional management agriculture in exurb regions. Furthermore, this paper constructs an analytical framework, which takes the“the adaptive reactions of the main body- elements changesenvironmental responses”as the mainline, to analyze the mechanism and characteristics of agricultural production system transition and its environmental effects from the dimensions of drawing force, supporting force and tractive force. The mechanism of the environmental effect of the transformation of the agricultural production system in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain is the disturbance to the agricultural ecosystem by the irrational input of capital, technology, and labor under the goal of increasing production and income and the constraints of regional natural conditions. The coupling patterns of agricultural production and their environmental effects are encapsulated into modern intensive agriculture in suburban regions with severe pollution, modern intensive agriculture in suburban regions with moderate pollution, modern intensive agriculture in exurb regions with severe pollution, and modern intensive agriculture in exurb regions with moderate pollution. In light of the results, policy recommendations are provided.

    Published English abstract

  10. Agricultural production transition and its environmental effects: Research progress and prospect

    张英男,龙花楼* (2022)

    自然资源学报, 37(07):1691-1706

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    The green transformation of agriculture has become an inevitable choice of rural vitalization and agricultural/rural reforms, therefore, it is urgent to explore the relationship between agricultural production transition and its environmental effects, and fuel the highquality development. In recent years, the process, spatio-temporal pattern and the mechanism of agricultural production transition and its environmental effects have been intensively investigated and discussed at multiple scales. In order to systematically review the progress and garner the research gaps, literature analysis was used to summarize the state- of- the- arts. Finally, this paper provided an overview of the research progress from the perspective of key elements of agricultural production, and then summarized the research progress of the environmental effects from three aspects - the identification of agricultural environmental problems, the relations between agricultural production transition and non- point source pollution, and agro-ecological efficiency. Future research of agricultural production transition and its environmental effects should be focused on explaining the mutual relations from system science, underlining the regional heterogeneity, enriching the farmland use transition research by applying land system science, and highlighting the micro-mechanism of the environmental response from the perspective of small-holding peasants in China.

    Published English abstract

  11. Research progress of urban-rural relations and its implications for rural revitalization

    张英男, 龙花楼*, 马历, 屠爽爽, 陈坤秋 (2019)

    地理研究, 38(03): 578-594

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    With the implementation of rural vitalization strategy, China has stepped into a critical period with the dramatic changes of urban- rural relations and the accelerating transformation development of rural territorial system. Scientifically understanding the research progress of urban-rural relation theory and evolution rule is of great significance for boosting rural vitalization, narrowing urban-rural disparity, adjusting urban-rural structure and optimizing urban- rural patterns. This paper elaborates the research progress of urban- rural relations and rural development in China from the dimensions of economy, society, ecology and culture based on the review of foreign urban- rural relations and the characteristics of domestic rural development, as well as the evolution of urban- rural relation. Furthermore, prospect of research focus or key fields in the future were given. Firstly, transforming the development idea from productivism oriented to post- productivism oriented and attaching importance to the multiple values of rural areas should be emphasized. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out intensive studies about the mechanism, regional path selection and development mode of rural vitalization based on the theory of rural multiple function transition. Understanding the relationship of different functions is essential for dealing with rural decline and realizing the comprehensive vitalization. Meanwhile, we should focus on the mechanism and format of rural vitalization based on different territorial types. Against the context of rural- urban integrated development, we should promote the supply- side reform and activate the forces of socioeconomic growth in underdeveloped areas. As for the developed rural areas, the“hybridity” should be emphasized and further studies should be conducted. In some rural areas, the phenomenon of the hybridity of development agents, the combination of production space and living space, the mixture of rurality and modernism have emerged. Accordingly, more emphasis should be placed on the heterogeneity and diversity in the process of rural restructuring. Secondly, with the emergence of new factors or new technologies, we should focus on the new morphology of rural development, such as characteristic towns, rural complex and“Taobao village”. In recent years, China's rural areas have undergone intensive restructuring motivated by e- commerce, which has triggered a new wave of rural rejuvenation. But how e- commerce affects rural development and the characteristics of this process are still unclear, and this is important for understanding the urban- rural relations under the context of informatization. Thirdly, the mechanism and format of urban- rural spatial restructuring should be emphasized. From the perspective of urban-rural interaction, the theory of urban-rural network may be practical and meaningful for optimizing the spatial distribution of infrastructure construction and industrial development. Lastly, creating or improving the theory and improving the path of rural vitalization according to the national conditions are meaningful for realizing the strategy.

    Published English abstract

  12. A Multidimensional Analysis of Rural Restructuring Driven by E-commerce: A Case of Xiaying Village in Central China

    张英男, 龙花楼*, 屠爽爽, 李裕瑞, 马历, 戈大专 (2019)

    地理科学, 39(06): 947-956

    Abstract

    In recent years, the boom of rural e-commerce in China has produced obvious effect on the morphology of economy, society and space in rural areas. Attempting to reveal the process and mechanism of rural restructuring driven by e-commerce, we applied semi-structural interview to depict and analyze the characteristics of this transition from the dimensions of economy, society and ecology. Moreover, we synthesized participatory rural appraisal and GIS techniques to map and quantitatively illustrate the spatial changes. Ultimately, the influential factors and characteristics of this pioneering undertaking were analyzed. The results showed dramatic changes in socio-economic morphology of Xiaying Village. Firstly, as for industrial mode, the pattern dominated by traditional agriculture has been transformed to that with a combination of the primary, secondary and tertiary industries. The industrial chain that integrates production, processing and selling has gradually formed, so that the industrial structure tends to be comprehensive and presents an ecological transition. Secondly, a growing number of young people who have become the mainstream of rural development get employed in non-agricultural industry, which indicates that rural e-commerce is an effective path for realizing situ urbanization. Rural e-commerce complicates the interest relationship among villagers and awakens their subject consciousness, thereby causing the increasing diversification of governance mainstream. In response, the trend of public service perfection, lifestyle modernization and social communication visualization becomes prominently. Thirdly, the element flows and their inherent physical movement resulted in the changes of their space carrier, concretely embodies in the gradual compression of agricultural production space and the intensive expansion of non-agricultural production space. Production-ecological compound space has experienced a sharp increase, and living space tends to be multifunctional and intensive. Fourthly, the industrial foundation of kallaite exploitation and processing plays a pivotal role in the process of rural restructuring in Xiaying Viallge. Besides, the e-commerce platform, logistics infrastructure, rural elites, resource endowments, as well as government support also function as the initial engine, resource support and external power. Finally, we analyzed the obstacles of rural restructuring and proposed some targeted countermeasures. Moreover, challenges and opportunities created by e-commerce for rural areas of inland and coastal areas were discussed, respectively.

    Published English abstract

  13. Spatio-temporal characteristics and dynamic mechanism of farmland functions evolution in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain

    张英男, 龙花楼*, 戈大专, 屠爽爽, 曲艺 (2018)

    地理学报, 73(03): 518-534

    [Publisher]
    Abstract

    Taking counties as the basic unit, this paper establishes the evaluation index system of farmland functions from the dimensions of economy, society and ecology, adopts the method combining entropy weighting and multiple correlation coefficient weighting to determine the weights, and calculates the farmland function indices of each county. Subsequently, the spatiotemporal characteristics of farmland functions evolution were analyzed and the coupling relationships between the sub- functions were explored based on the coupling coordination model, simultaneously, the dynamic mechanism of farmland functions evolution was quantitatively probed by applying the spatial econometric regression analysis method in this research. Major conclusions were drawn as follows: (1) The farmland economic function generally presented a declining trend during 1990- 2010. Especially, the function is strengthened in underdeveloped and agriculture dominated counties, and weakened continuously in developed areas on contrary; 60.29% of the counties decrease in farmland social function, whereas some counties, which are mostly located in the north of Zhengzhou, the west of Dezhou and Cangzhou, Yantai and Weihai, have experienced an obvious increase; The dramatic decline of farmland ecological function has occurred around Beijing, Tianjin and Jinan. Areas located in northern Henan Province and central Shandong Province has witnessed an increase of ecological function. (2) There is a significant spatial difference in the coupling degree and coordination degree of the sub- functions, and the decoupling phenomenon gradually highlights. The changes of social function and ecological function lag behind those of economic function in developed areas, but they are highly coupled in some underdeveloped areas. (3) The evolution of farmland functions in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain resulted from the comprehensive effects of regional basic conditions and external driving factors. Furthermore, the transition of population and industry in the process of urbanization and industrialization plays a decisive role in evolution intensity and direction of farmland sub- systems including economy, society and ecology. According to the results above mentioned, agricultural modernization, industrialization and promoting the transformation of traditional agriculture should be regarded as an important engine driving the sustainable development of Huang-Huai- Hai Plain. In view of regional differentiation characteristics of farmland functions evolution, differentiated and diversified farmland use and management modes should be implemented from developed urban areas to underdeveloped traditional agricultural areas.

Research projects

Research and consultancy · Led and participating projects
NSFC · General Program · 42671257

Responses and adaptation of protected agriculture under climate risk stress: Perspectives from greenhouse farming

2027–2030 · Principal investigator · Starts January 2027

This project examines how climate risks reshape the spatial distribution of protected agriculture and the livelihoods and production decisions of greenhouse farmers. It traces the links between thermal suitability, spatial reconfiguration and household adaptation, treating protected agriculture as both vulnerable to climate shocks and a means of adapting to them. Combining large language model–assisted semantic analysis, double machine learning and scenario projections, the research seeks to identify effective adaptation pathways and avoid maladaptation. Its aim is to support climate-resilient greenhouse farming and a diversified food supply system.

NSFC · Young Scientists Fund · 42201204

Examining the driving mechanism, multiple effects and improvement strategies of the commodification of spatial resources in rural China: A case study of the typical villages in Zhejiang Province

2022–2025 · Principal investigator · Project period ended December 2025

Using typical villages in Zhejiang Province as case studies, this project investigates how rural spatial resources are commodified and how this process changes land values, income distribution and local governance. A power–capital–local analytical framework, grounded in the production of space theory, guides qualitative and quantitative analysis of the interaction between public authority, investment and community actors. By examining stakeholders’ experiences alongside observable changes, the research develops governance and policy approaches to reduce adverse effects and support rural revitalization and shared prosperity.

Books

Authored and edited volumes
SPRINGER · 2026 · Sustainable Development Goals Series

Transforming Agriculture, Farmland Use and the Environment in China

Yingnan Zhang & Hualou Long · Co-authors

This book examines the interactions between agricultural transformation, farmland use and environmental change in China. Drawing on complex adaptive systems theory and national and regional evidence, it connects changing agricultural practices with population mobility, technological adoption, market forces and policy interventions. Across six parts and twenty chapters, the analysis combines qualitative research, statistical methods and system dynamics to explain spatial patterns, environmental consequences and possible future trajectories. It concludes with policy approaches for aligning agricultural productivity, sustainable land management and rural development.

Publisher
FORTHCOMING · ROUTLEDGEThe Making of
Commodified
Rural ChinaYingnan ZhangOfficial cover forthcoming
ROUTLEDGE · FORTHCOMING

The Making of Commodified Rural China

Yingnan Zhang · Author

Drawing on sustained fieldwork in Beijing, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Sichuan and Hubei, this book investigates how agriculture, land, ecological resources and rural spaces become commodities. It brings the production of space theory into dialogue with comparative village research to examine the interaction of the state, capital and local communities. Through cases involving greenhouse farming, digital platforms, land market reform and ecological value creation, the book explores how rural transformation redistributes benefits and reshapes governance. Its central concern is how institutional arrangements can reconcile market efficiency with community interests and more equitable rural development.

Forthcoming. Synopsis only.

CHINA LAND PRESS · 2023 · CHINESE-LANGUAGE VOLUME

International Cooperation on Natural Resources

Yingnan Zhang · Deputy Editor-in-Chief

This volume introduces international cooperation on natural resources through the interconnected fields of mineral resources, marine resources and global ecology. It traces the evolution of resource relations from competition and trade toward cooperative governance, examining the institutions and agreements that shape resource use and environmental protection. The discussion situates China’s participation within wider debates on sustainable development, shared global challenges and mutually beneficial cooperation. Designed as part of a natural resources management series, the book offers a foundation for understanding why international collaboration matters for resource security and ecological sustainability.

Fieldwork in China

Select a numbered point or a village below to explore the case. Markers indicate approximate county/district-level locations.

Basemap: Alibaba Cloud DataV · South China Sea islands shown in inset.

Zhoucun Village

Jiangning District, Nanjing, Jiangsu

Tourism, government and capital

A peri-urban tourism case combining agricultural sightseeing, heritage and hospitality. Research examines how government intervention and successive forms of capital shape its commodification trajectory.

Zhongxin Village

Zhijin County, Bijie, Guizhou

Seasonal tourism and capital constraints

A comparative case of blossom-oriented rural tourism. Its seasonal development illustrates the challenges of sustaining investment and diversifying rural commodity economies.

Jingshan Village

Yuhang District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang

Tea culture and collaborative governance

Tea production and Buddhist pilgrimage culture underpin this case. It explores how rural commodification changes relationships among government, enterprises, village collectives and residents.

Xiaying Village

Yunxi County, Shiyan, Hubei

E-commerce and platform-mediated restructuring

A mountain village connected to national markets through e-commerce. The case examines returning migrants, local resources, public infrastructure and platforms in rural economic restructuring.

Zhinan Village

Linan District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang

Mountain landscapes and rural tourism

Zhinan is a mountain village in Taihuyuan, Linan, known for terraced fields, ancient trees, historic paths and a village pond. Rural tourism links these landscapes with homestays and farm-based hospitality, offering a case of how natural and cultural amenities support village livelihoods.

Case background: Ministry of Culture and Tourism ↗

Lizu Village

Yiwu, Jinhua, Zhejiang

Young entrepreneurs moving to the countryside

Lizu attracts young entrepreneurs through shared workspaces, business incubation and professional village operations. Craft studios, cultural businesses and tourism services connect newcomers with village resources. Cooperation among the village collective, the operating company and entrepreneurs provides a case of youth-led rural renewal.

Case background: Zhejiang CPPCC · People’s Political Consultative Daily ↗

Zhanqi Village

Pidu District, Chengdu, Sichuan

Rural land institutions and collective development

Zhanqi is a case of rural land reform centred on the market entry of collectively owned commercial construction land. Alongside collective property-rights and shareholding reforms, it connects land assets with investment and rural industries, illustrating how institutional change can reshape collective economic development.

Case background: National Development and Reform Commission ↗
